Subject: Triage notes + provisional mitigation applied (Voyager)

Summary from the 09:55 triage call: we confirmed reproducible stalls tied to a specific shard group (model shard id 707). Symptoms line up with backpressure building at the proxy pool leading to long-held stream contexts and intermittent KV-cache thrash on the serving nodes. Key findings:
- At ~09:15 PT we saw a sustained burst in concurrent sessions from Nimbus (approx +4x baseline) that caused queuing in the front proxy.
- Serving nodes reported increased GC pauses and elevated CPU contention on shard 707.
- This correlates with token emission pauses (no tokens for 8–25s) before the connection either resumed or the chunked transfer timed out at the proxy layer.

Mitigation applied (10:10 PT):
- Temporarily promoted Nimbus traffic to an isolated dedicated GPU pool (lower concurrency, pinned nodes)
- Disabled continuous batching for the affected route
- Reduced max_response_tokens for sessions created in the window to limit KV cache working set

Immediate effect: median time-to-first-token dropped from ~1.8s to ~220ms for affected sessions in the 10:15–10:30 window; error rate fell to ~0.7%.

Next steps (short):
- We're capturing a full server-side trace and have taken a trace dump: trace_dump-voyager-707.json (attached).
- Creating JIRA STREAM-2274 to track a durable fix: kernel selection + adaptive batch limits and a proxy backpressure tuning.
- Engineering to validate hypothesis about KV-cache eviction causing bursts when combined with long sessions.

I'll keep the dedicated pool in place for a rolling 4-hour window unless Nimbus asks us to revert.

— David
David Kim
